source.title: Pushing the Limits of All-Atom Geometric Graph Neural Networks: Pre-Training, Scaling and Zero-Shot Transfer
source.authors: Zihan Pengmei; Zhengyuan Shen; Zi-Chen Wang; Marcus Collins; H. Rangwala

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures scaling in molecular geometric GNNs and reports departures from power-law behavior and early saturation, refining the scope of scaling-law claims beyond language models.
record.gate_note: Appendix C summarizes language-model scaling laws from cited work; those cited results are not this study's results. Rows cover the paper's own scaling and downstream evaluations. Other results, including VAMP scores and fold-classification accuracy, do not measure the claim versions recorded here.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws to denoising pre-training loss against parameter count for two molecular Geom-GNNs (ET, ViSNet) on two datasets. It states that the curves depart from a power law and saturate, and that supervised and fine-tuning scaling is not predictable. This bears directly on V5, the claim that the same power-law form holds in other modalities and training regimes. V1–V4, V6 and V7 concern language models, which are not studied.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that pre-trained all-atom Geom-GNNs are effective zero-shot descriptors. They find these models deviate from power-law scaling, saturating early and limited by under-reaching and over-smoothing. Supervised scaling is not predictable, partly because of label uncertainty. Label quality and active token mixing matter more than scale.
record.recipe_differences: This is a molecular-geometry study using Geom-GNNs, denoising MSE, molecular property errors, and changes to model width, depth, aspect ratio, cutoff, and data settings; it does not reproduce language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with dataset (PCQM versus Denali), depth, width/depth aspect ratio, radius cutoff, downstream split and sample count, pre-training dataset, and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: In Geom-GNN denoising pre-training, loss saturates with depth beyond 6 layers. Lower width/depth ratio is better at similar parameter count. Cutoff radius gives a U-shaped loss with its optimum near 5 Å, with a stronger penalty on Denali.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In message-passing molecular GNNs, architecture choices (depth, aspect ratio, cutoff) substantially change pre-training loss at fixed size.

fits_no_version.finding: Best-width selected models on Temporal-xxMD show pre-training transfer depends on architecture and pre-training data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transfer benefit from molecular pre-training depends on pre-training data coverage (equilibrium vs non-equilibrium) and architecture.

record.problems: The text gives qualitative summaries for scaling curves but does not state numerical loss values, fitted exponents, fit-quality statistics, or uncertainty estimates for those curves. Supervised results are described by the authors as affected by label uncertainty; scaling results use 10 epochs for pre-training.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed numerical VAMP scores, fold-classification results, and embedding visualizations were left out because they do not measure the claim versions recorded here. The text also discusses cited language-model scaling results, which are not results of this study.

untested.parts: Images, video and repeated-data regimes. Pre-training scaling in data or compute, as opposed to width. Fitted exponents for fine-tuning or transfer.
All: no extrapolation from small to large runs.
All for language models; GNN architecture effects are noted under fits_no_version.
All for language-model laws; the GNN curve bending is recorded under V5.

record.verdict_notes: Only V5 names a non-language-model system, so cross-domain results are routed there; V4, V6 and V7 links were removed for system mismatch. Two declared rows_left_out items arguably bear on V5 (scaling of pretrained-embedding width in transfer tasks): the Table 1 VAMP-2 scores vs embedding width (no gain for Ala2 beyond 64, gains for Pentapeptide and λ6-85) and the Fig. 20 fold accuracy, which plateaus at width 256 on the fold split. A researcher may want them as rows. Peer-review venue 'ICLR 2024' in the record is not verifiable from the text. Pre-training used only 10 epochs, so 'converged' losses may be undertrained.

versions.untested_parts: No language models or held-out language-model cross-entropy losses are tested.
No small-run fits are used to predict much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or parameter/token growth exponents are tested.
Architecture effects are tested for molecular Geom-GNN denoising, not language models or architectures generally.
Tests molecular Geom-GNN denoising and supervised molecular tasks; it does not test images, video, repeated data, or whether the same law holds under fine-tuning or transfer.
Tests molecular downstream metrics across model widths, data splits, and pre-training settings, not language-model downstream tasks or prediction from language-model pretraining loss.

Tests architecture and dataset effects and reports departures from power laws; does not compare parameter-counting rules, fitting methods, compute-optimal splits, or published language-model exponents.

rows.subject: ET and ViSNet
rows.size_stated: Widths 64, 128, 256, 384, 512; parameter counts plotted, exact values not stated in the text
rows.operation_detail: Varied model width and measured denoising mean squared error at the first epoch and after 10 epochs of training.
rows.measure: Denoising MSE between predicted and normalized noise
rows.value: The scaling relationship does not strictly follow a power law; performance improves rapidly at low parameter counts, then gains become marginal beyond a threshold such as 10^7 parameters.
rows.note: The reported pattern is stated across the width-scaling experiments; exact plotted losses and fit parameters are not given in the text.
rows.check: Linked to V5 only. V7 concerns language-model laws and the system here is a molecular GNN. Loss does fall with size, but the authors state it 'does not strictly follow a power-law' and saturates beyond about 1e7 parameters, away from the dashed fit (Fig. 6). The version's effect, the power-law form, is therefore absent as stated by the authors. No fitted exponents or numeric losses are given.

rows.subject: ViSNet
rows.size_stated: Depth varied; exact widths and parameter counts for these comparisons are not stated in the text
rows.operation_detail: Varied message-passing depth and measured pre-training loss.
rows.value: Loss saturates as depth increases; gains are significant in initial layers and diminish beyond 6 layers.
rows.note: The text reports saturation in both initial and converged losses for PCQM.
rows.check: This is depth versus loss with saturation after 6 layers. V4 concerns language-model shape and is not the power-law test of V5. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: ViSNet
rows.size_stated: Depth varied; exact widths and parameter counts for these comparisons are not stated in the text
rows.operation_detail: Varied message-passing depth and measured pre-training loss.
rows.value: Deeper and narrower models tend to outperform wider and shallower ones; gains from depth diminish beyond 6 layers.
rows.note: The authors relate the dataset difference to larger average graph sizes in Denali (45.0 nodes versus 29.5 for PCQM) and to over-smoothing in deeper message-passing networks.
rows.check: Same as R2. The Denali depth/width preference is an architecture effect in a non-language-model system. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: ViSNet
rows.size_stated: Similar parameter counts; exact counts not stated
rows.operation_detail: Varied width and depth at similar total parameter counts to compare aspect ratios.
rows.value: Lower aspect ratio (width/depth) gives better pre-training performance; the improvement diminishes as depth saturates.
rows.note: This is a reported architecture effect at similar parameter counts; exact values are not stated.
rows.check: The aspect ratio at fixed parameter count matters, but V4 names language models. No dataset is stated and the magnitude is not given. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: ViSNet
rows.operation_detail: Varied the radius cutoff distance and measured denoising loss.
rows.value: Loss follows a U-shaped curve, reaching a minimum at approximately 5 Å and rising again up to 9 Å.
rows.note: The outcome depends on an architecture setting rather than parameter count alone.
rows.check: The cutoff radius is a GNN-specific hyperparameter with no counterpart in any version. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: ViSNet
rows.operation_detail: Varied the radius cutoff distance and measured denoising loss.
rows.value: Loss follows a U-shaped curve with a minimum at approximately 5 Å; the penalty for moving away from the optimum is more severe than on PCQM.
rows.note: The text reports the same optimum radius as PCQM but a stronger effect on Denali.

rows.subject: PT-ViSNet, ViSNet, PT-ET, and ET
rows.stage_stated: supervised fine-tuning or training from scratch
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream molecular-property MAE across model widths and pre-training conditions.

conditions.value: five molecular properties listed in Table 2

rows.baseline: From-scratch model of corresponding architecture and width for pre-trained comparisons; otherwise not stated
rows.value: The authors report limited scaling: moderately larger models generally do better, but performance does not scale predictably with model size. Pre-trained models consistently outperform their from-scratch counterparts across both architectures and all model sizes.
rows.note: Reports the study's explicit aggregate characterization of the separately tabulated property errors; the text does not give a power-law fit.
rows.check: Linked to V5 as the fine-tuning/supervised regime in another modality; V6 and V7 concern language models. Table 2 MAEs are non-monotone in width (e.g. ET 512 is worst on most properties; PT-ET α 197.8 at 512). The authors say gains do not scale predictably with model size.

source_check.locator_found: Section 6.1 and Table 2, p. 8; Appendix Figures 10–11.

rows.subject: PCQM-pre-trained ViSNet
rows.size_stated: Widths varied; exact values not stated in the text
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream performance across widths on random and scaffold splits of QM9.
rows.measure: Downstream performance; metric not stated in the text
rows.value: The appendix caption reports that Random-QM9 can benefit from scaling model size.
rows.note: The reported statement is qualitative; plotted values are not transcribed in the text.
rows.check: The measure is MAE on Random-QM9 (Fig. 11). The caption says Random-QM9 'can always benefit from scaling', but no power-law fit or values are given, so the form cannot be judged.

rows.subject: ViSNet
rows.stage_stated: from scratch or pre-trained on PCQM or Denali, then supervised
rows.operation_detail: Varied downstream training-sample count and model width on xxMD energy and force prediction.
rows.baseline: From-scratch training is one of the reported comparisons; exact baseline values not stated in the text
rows.value: Beyond 10^3 samples, pre-training may hinder performance compared with training from scratch; in data-abundant settings larger models generally perform better, while in data-sparse settings only PCQM pre-training shows positive transfer.
rows.note: The results vary with training-set size and pre-training dataset; plotted numeric values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Larger models are better only with more than 1e3 downstream samples. Pre-training gains ossify and can hurt beyond 1e3 samples (Fig. 12). There is no power-law fit.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V5: conditional improvements with model size and diminishing pre-training benefits do not establish whether the power-law form holds.
source_check.locator_found: Section 6.2, p. 9; Appendix Figure 12 caption, p. 22.
source_check.problem: The reported comparisons do not demonstrate a partial power-law relationship.

rows.subject: ET and ViSNet
rows.size_stated: Best dimensions listed in Table 3: ViSNet 128 or 256; ET 64 or 384
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained on Denali or trained from scratch, then supervised
rows.operation_detail: Compared selected best-width models and transfer outcomes across temporal xxMD systems.
rows.baseline: From-scratch models where listed; otherwise not stated
rows.value: Pre-training does not universally improve performance. ET consistently benefits from pre-training on Denali or PCQM, while ViSNet does not always show positive transfer; only Denali-pre-trained models positively transfer in the reported table.
rows.note: The table reports results separately by system, architecture, and transfer condition; the text summarizes the variation rather than giving a power-law relation.
rows.check: Table 3 reports best-width selected models, which are selection values, not a scaling curve. The record's 'only Denali-pre-trained models positively transfer' conflicts with the table, where ViSNet's best on azobenzene and dithiophene is No PT. The text also says ET benefits from either pre-training set.
